Title: Sancti Eusebii Hieronymi Epistulae, pars I: Epistulae I-LXX (Corpus Scriptorum Ecclesiasticorum Latinorum, vol. LIV)
Creator: Jerome (c. 347-420), with the letters he received and translated; edited by Isidor Hilberg (title page)
Publisher: Vindobonae, Lipsiae: F. Tempsky, G. Freytag (title page)
Publication Date: 1910 (title page, host OCR line 47, misread as 'MDC/cCCX.'; the preface is signed 'Cernouiciis, mense Februario anni MCMX', host line 138)
Rights: Public Domain (pd-us-by-date: published 1910); the archive.org record gives possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. The scan carries no notice against reproduction.
Language: lat
Source: archive.org item corpusscriptorum54stuoft (University of Toronto copy), full text from the item's own djvu.txt at https://archive.org/download/corpusscriptorum54stuoft/corpusscriptorum54stuoft_djvu.txt. Fetched directly 2026-11-26 by the era 1 Library session (Church Family Tree); the byte count of the downloaded file (1,813,993) equals the size archive.org lists for the djvu.txt.
Provenance note: Extracted unaltered: the item's own djvu.txt is reproduced whole after this header; nothing was stripped, normalized or corrected. Line numbers cited in this header are lines of the host OCR: host line N is line N + 12 of this file. OCR quality: the Latin is good, with doubled spacing between words as scanned and some letters misread (r for n, l for I in places); the apparatus is run in below each page. Rights basis restated: Public Domain (pd-us-by-date: published 1910).
Content note: Hilberg's critical Latin text of Jerome's Letters 1 to 70, with apparatus. Letter 51, 'Epistula Epiphanii Cypri missa ad Iohannem episcopum a sancto Hieronymo translata', begins at host OCR line 19861: Epiphanius of Salamis to John of Jerusalem, in Jerome's Latin, made from Epiphanius's Greek, which does not survive. The ordination of Paulinianus in 'ecclesia uillae, quae est iuxta monasterium nostrum' is at about host lines 19958-19970; the charge against Origen, 'Arrii patrem et aliarum hereseon radicem et parentem', at about host line 20102. This is the Latin original of Fremantle's English in npnf206. Check every quotation against the page images before it passes.

Quamquam  huius  editionis  rationemconsiliilmquetotodemum 
opere  ad  finem  perducto  ea,  qua  par  erit,  diligentia  expositurus 
sum,  tamen  iam  huic  primo  uolumini  pauca  quaedam  prae- 
mittenda  sunt.  Et  primum  quidem  eos,  qui  hac  editione 
utuntur,  scire  uolo  alterum  eius  uolumen  (=  uol.  LV)  con- 
tinens  epistulas  LXXI — CXX  anno  1911  proditurum  esse; 
tertium  autem  (=  uol.  LVI),  cui  inerunt  reliquae  epistulae, 
indices,  prolegomena,  duobus  annis  post  publici  fiet  iuris. 

In  uerbis  Hieronymi  constituendis  coniecturis  raro  opus 
erat;  quodsi  huius  editionis  textus  nihilo  minus  satis  differt 
a  textu  uulgato,  id  inde  repetendum  est,  quod  mihi  libros  manu 
scriptos  perscrutanti  et  aut  primo  in  usum  uocanti  aut,  '  ni 
fallor,  rectius  aestimanti  uberrimi  laetissimique  fructus  pro- 
uenerunt.  In  rebus  orthographicis  omisso  omni  aequabilitatis 
studio  optimos  codices  sequi  satius  duxi.  Inter  codices,  qui 
alicuius  pretii  habendi  sunt,  ne  unus  quidem  omnes  epistulas 
conplectitur:  exstant  satis  ampla  corpora  epistularum  selec- 
tarum,  exstant  codices,  quorum  singuli  conplures  uel  paucis- 
simas  tantummodo  epistulas  continent,  exstant  denique  excerpta 
quaedam  ex  epistulis  Hieronymianis  saeculo  iam  sexto  con- 
fecta,  quorum  tamen  pretium  scribarum  licentia  ualde  minuitur. 
Neque  ea  est  codicum  condicio,  ut  unus  saltem  uel  alter  inter- 
polationibus  prorsus  careat;  immo  etiam  in  uetustissimis  libris 
locos  deprehendimus  uel  interpolatos  uel  grauiter  corruptos. 
Adde  quod  satis  saepe  eiusdem  codicis  singulae  partes  non 
eiusdem  sunt  pretii.  Sigla,  quibus  singulos  codices  notaui, 
satis  multa,  sed  ita  conparata  sunt,  ut  per  totius  editionis 
ambitum  singuli  libri  manu  scripti  eadem  semper  nota  signi- 
ficentur.  Lectiones  superiorum  editionum  siglo  g  conprehendere
